summary: P2's three wires — notifications to Alertmanager, direct-to-Keycloak SSO, and the ESO-materialised credentials — all land, and the design's load-bearing claims hold when checked against Argo CD v3.5.1's own code and the live estate (part-of label, both webhook receivers resolving $refs, repo-creds prefix matching, the openbao-prd store and the eso/prd/* grant). Nothing is tagged blocking. Three advisory findings ride along: a startup window in which the applicationset-controller can cache the unresolved webhook reference forever, a mutation-proven blind spot in the new requestedScopes assertion, and a comment naming the wrong repo for the estate's shared ESO helper.

findings.summary: The applicationset-controller builds its GitHub webhook handler once at startup and never re-reads settings, so if it starts before ESO materialises argocd-webhook it verifies deliveries against the literal $argocd-webhook:githubSecret until the pod is restarted.
render-chart.py's `"groups" not in oidc.get("requestedScopes", [])` passes when the key is deleted — the exact regression it guards; mutation run, gate stayed green at exit 0.
external-secrets.yaml's header says the estate's shared ExternalSecret helper lives in HelmCharts; it is defined in Charts' homelab-shared library chart.
